# 俱舍論實義疏

**ID:** T1561
**Volume:** T29
**Category:** 毘曇部類
**Original Category:** 毘曇部
**Byline:** 尊者安惠造
**Juans:** 5
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1561

## Contributors
- 安慧 (A000371)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Jùshě Lùn Shíyì Shū* 俱舍論實義疏 (Skt. *Abhidharmakośa-ṭīkā-tattvārtha*; CBETA T29n1561) is a 5-juan Chinese-language commentary on Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośa* ([KR6l0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6l/KR6l0023)), attributed to the Indian Yogācāra master Sthiramati 尊者悉地羅末底 ([安慧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E6%85%A7), Chinese 安惠/安慧). The text's opening attribution reads "尊者悉地羅末底造(唐言安惠)" — "composed by the venerable Sthiramati (rendered in Chinese as Ānhuì)." The catalog lists only CBETA and 【大】 as editions, with no dynasty and no translator. The translator's identity and the date of translation are unknown; it may represent a lost Tang or pre-Tang transmission.

**Abstract**

Sthiramati 安慧 (Skt. *Sthiramati* "Fixed Wisdom"; Chinese 安慧 *Ānhuì* / 安惠 *Ānhuì*; c. late 5th–early 6th century CE) was a major Yogācāra philosopher of the post-Vasubandhu period, active in Valabhī (伐臘毗國, western India). He was a student of [德慧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%85%A7) *Guṇamati* and is characterized as a contemporary and predecessor of [護法](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%B7%E6%B3%95) (*Dharmapāla*, 530–561 CE) in the *Chéngyùshí lùn shùjì* 成唯識論述記 ([KR6n0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0026)). He composed commentaries on Vasubandhu's works in both the Abhidharma and Yogācāra traditions, including a major commentary on the *Trimśikā* (《唯識三十頌釋論》) and the present commentary on the *Kośa*.

The present text is a partial or compressed commentary (*ṭīkā*) on the *Kośa*, covering the text chapter by chapter. It reflects Sthiramati's Yogācāra perspective — treating the *Kośa* from within the intellectual framework later elaborated in the *Madhyānta-vibhāga* and *Trimśikā* traditions — in contrast to the strictly Vaibhāṣika reading favored by the Kaśmīri Sarvāstivādins. A Tibetan version of Sthiramati's *Kośa* commentary survives in the Tengyur (Tōhoku 4122). The Chinese rendering is incomplete and its translation history uncertain.
